issues.legal_issue: A customary appointment as heir outside a person’s natural family does not, by itself, extinguish the appointee’s right to inherit from collaterals in the natural family.
material_facts: The predecessor of the claimants had been appointed as heir by his maternal uncle under the community’s custom.
The claimants, as descendants of the appointee, sought to inherit property belonging to a collateral in the appointee’s natural family.
The claim did not concern inheritance from the appointee’s natural father in the presence of natural brothers.
issues.conclusion: The customary appointment did not exclude the appointee’s descendants from inheriting from collaterals in his natural family.
issues.legal_principle: Under the general custom stated in Article 48 of Rattigan’s Digest, an heir appointed in another family ordinarily retains the right to succeed to property in the natural family as against collaterals. The exception is inheritance from the natural father in the presence of natural brothers, who take to the exclusion of the appointed heir and his descendants. The court relied on Mela Singh v. Gurdas, Jagat Singh v. Ishar Singh, Kanshi Ram v. Situ, Rahmat v. Ziledar, and Jai Kapur v. Sher Singh.

predicates.customary_inheritance_dispute: The proceeding concerns a claim to inheritance governed by customary law.
predicates.customary_heir_appointed_outside_natural: A person was appointed as heir under custom by someone outside that person’s natural family.
predicates.claim_concerns_natural_family_collateral: The claim is to property of a collateral in the appointee’s natural family, rather than to the natural father’s property in the presence of natural brothers.

issues.definition: When a customary inheritance dispute concerns an appointee’s natural-family collaterals, an appointee chosen as heir outside the natural family retains the right to inherit from those collaterals.

issues.legal_issue: A local customary record does not displace the general custom on collateral inheritance when it addresses only direct inheritance from the natural father and no contrary local custom is proved.
material_facts: The local customary record addressed whether an adopted son could inherit from his natural father and stated that he could not inherit directly, while recognizing an entitlement to property that would come to the adoptive father as a collateral.
The record did not address inheritance from collaterals in the natural family.

The cited instances of exclusion concerned inheritance in the presence of natural brothers or an uncontested transfer following a daughter’s remarriage, and did not establish a contrary custom governing collateral inheritance.
The party asserting a local custom that excluded the claimants did not establish that custom.
issues.conclusion: The local customary record and cited instances did not establish a special custom excluding the claimants from collateral inheritance, so the general custom applied.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the Punjab Laws Act, 1872 makes an applicable, established custom the rule of decision and otherwise applies personal law; the party asserting custom must prove both its applicability and content, as stated in Daya Ram v. Sohel Singh and affirmed in Abdul Hussain Khan v. Bibi Sona Dero. A local Riwaj-i-am ordinarily has an initial presumption of correctness and prevails over conflicting general custom, but the court found no relevant conflict here; it relied on Jai Kapur v. Sher Singh. Article 48 of Rattigan’s Digest records the general custom preserving an appointed heir’s right against collaterals in the natural family.

predicates.customary_inheritance_dispute: The proceeding concerns a claim to inheritance governed by customary law.
predicates.local_customary_record_addresses_direct_: The local customary record concerns whether an appointed heir may inherit directly from the natural father.
predicates.no_proven_local_rule_on_collateral_inher: The evidence does not establish a local customary rule excluding an appointed heir or descendants from inheritance from collaterals in the natural family.

issues.definition: In a customary inheritance dispute, where the local record concerns only direct inheritance from the natural father and no local rule on collateral inheritance is proved, the general custom governs collateral inheritance.
